Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR PRIMARY LEVEL
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 September 1980, after the draft finalized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 Primary level is a high precision level used for first order levelling operations. These operations include precision height measurements for topographical maps; engineering works, such as tunneling, installation of heavy machinery, hydroelectric projects, etc; height determination for geophysical purposes; gravity reductions, measuring the departure of mean sea level from a single equipotential surface and to record changes of height, 0.3 Primary level (see Fig. 1 ) mainly consists of an internal focussing telescope having high magnification and high resolution. The level is fitted with a parallel glass plate mounted in front of objective lens and a built in optical micrometer to measure the fraction of a levelling staff graduation interval. These levels are normally of two types, namely, tilting level and automatic level. The tilting level is one in which the axis is approximately levelled with a small circular bubble and more accurate levelling is done by centring a more sensitive bubble by means of a tilting screw. The automatic type is one in which the axis is approximately levelled by a circular bubble and more accurate levelling is achieved automatically by a prism system suspended under gravity inside the instrument. This standard deals with the tilting type level. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies the requirements of tilting type primary level capable of attaining standard deviation ( mean square error ) of & O-20 mm in 1 km of double levelling. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions given in IS : 1399-1959* shall apply. *Glossary of terms used in optical technology. definitions and the

The rocking motion to this plate displaces the light rays entering the objective of telescope and thereby enables measurement of the fraction of a levelling staff graduation interval. 3. 3.7.1 The level shall be provided with a rocking The rocking plate shall be an optically plane parallel a tube and mounted in front of the objective.

3.7.2 The rocking plate shall be capable of rotating by means of a mechanical micrometer drum fitted outside. The micrometer drum shall be graduated and figured as given under 3.9.1 (n) to (r). A magnifier shall be provided to view the micrometer readings. 3.7.3 Alternatively, an optical micrometer shall preferably be provided internally. It shall be connected with the rocking plate by mechanical arrangements. The micrometer scale shall be engraved and figured on a glass plate as given under 3.9.1 (n) to (r) and provision shall be made to project its readings optically in the field of view of the telescope. The micrometer and the rocking plate shall be capable of rotating by means of an external knob. An eyepiece shall be provided to view the projected micrometer readings. 3.8 Telescope focussing coating

3.8.1 The telescope shall be provided with an internal arrangement and its optics shall be provided with antireflection conforming to IS : 8248-1976*.

3.8.2 The graticule of the telescope shall be provided with cross and stadia lines, the latter being provided in the vertical cross line. The distances of stadia lines from the horizontal cross line shall be equal. The gracicule lines shall be made on optically Aat glass plate. Provision shall be made to move the graticule plate precisely for adjusting collimation easily in the laboratory as well as in the field. 3.8.3 The telescope for slow motion in the in the vertical plane. and figured suitably to shall be provided with a clamping screw, a screw horizontal plane and a tilting screw for slow tilting The head of the tilting screw shall be graduated facilitate adjustment of bubbles as given in 5.2.1.1. shall be provided on the telescope for

5.1.4.1 Clear aperture - The clear aperture of the objective shall be The measured value measured by a slide gauge or any suitable device. shall conform to the specified value. 5.1.4.2 Bubbles -The sensitivity, consistency and all other parameters of the bubbles shall be tested in accordance with 6.1 to 6.7 of IS : 1632-1960* and the values so obtained shall conform to the specified values within the tolerances laid down in Table II of IS : 1632-1960*. 5.1.5
Optical

5.1.5.1 Graticules alignment - The alignment of the graticule shall be tested with the help of a collimator and any misalignment shall be corrected by seeing the collimator's graticule.

5.1.5.2 Definition - The definition of the telescope shall be tested with the help of a definition board given in Appendix E of IS : 2754-19647. The circles, lines and squares of the board shall appear sharply defined without any distortion and colour over atleast two-thirds of the field of view. The definition and freedom from colour and distortion over the remaining field shall also be reasonably satisfactory, 5.1.5.3 MagniJication - The magnification of the telescope shall be tested by the method specified in Appendix C of IS : 2754-1964t. The measured value shall not differ by more than 5 percent from the specified value. 5.1.5.4 Resolving power - The resolving power of the telescope shall be measured by the method specified in Appendix F of IS: 2754-1964t. The measured value shall not differ by more than 5 percent from the theoretical value. 5.1.5.5 Field of view - The field of view of the telescope shall be tested by the method specified in Appendix D of IS : 2754-1964t. The measured value shall not differ by more than 5 percent of the specified value. 5.1.5.6 Parallax-The level shall be tested for parallax with the help of a collimator. After levelling the instrument with the help of two bubbles, the telescope shall be focussed on the collimator's graticule. There shall not be any apparent movement between the image of the
*Specification for bubbles. tGeneral requirements for optical instruments.

9

IS:9613-1980 collimator's graticule and the telescope's graticule on viewing the former through the eyepiece and moving eye at right angles to the axis of eyepiece. 5.1.5.7 Collimation - The collimation shall be tested in the laboratory with the help of a collimator. The instrument shall be accurately levelled with the help of the two bubbles ( see Note ) provided and the collimator's graticule shall be focussed by it. Any deviation in the coincidence of image of the collimator's graticule and telescope graticule shall represent collimation error. This shall be corrected by moving the graticule with the help of adjusting screws provided in its mount.
NOTE-The bubbles shall be first adjusted as given in 5.2.1.1.

5.1.5.8 Strain - The optics of the telescope shall be free from strain. It shall be tested as under: The level shall be so held that its telescope is in the path of light between two crossed nicols in a sensitive polariscope or strain viewer. The strain present in the telescope shall be revealed by the colour of the transmitted light. Before introducing the telescope of the level, the nicols shall be set for magenta colour. The strained areas in the optics of the telescope shall not show colour beyond indigo in the optical spectrum. 5.2 Operational Tests 5.2.1 General 5.2.1.1 Bubbles - The instrument shall be placed on a perfectly flat and firm surface. The telescope shall be put parallel to any two foot screws facing the observer and the instrument shall be levelled by these two foot screws using the cylindrical bubble only. The bubble shall be seen in U-shape in this situation. This shall be called the first position. The telescope shall then be rotated through 90" from this position in the clockwise direction and levelled ( U-shape made ) with the help of the third The telescope foot screw only. This shall be called the second position. shall then be rotated through 90" from the second position in clockwise direction SO that it becomes again parallel to the first two foot screws as in the beginning ( first position ). The instrument shall then be levelled by making U-shape of the bubble, half with the help of two foot screws and half by using the tilting screw of the telescope. This process shall be repeated ( that is to level in the first position, half by two footscrews parallel to telescope and half by tilting screw while in the second position by the third foot screw only ) till the cylindrical bubble is perfectly levelled in all the positions of the telescope ( that is U-shape is not disturbed in all the positions of the telescope ). 10

1s : 9613- 1980
The circular bubble shall then be brought in centre with the help of its adjusting screws without using footscrews and tilting screw till it remains in centre in all the positions of the instrument. 5.2.1.2
Reading accuracies:

a) The instrument

shall be focussed on an appropriate vertical staff and the readings with the three graticule lines shall be taken. The mean of the three readings shall agree with the middle line readings within 0.6 mm. b) The height difference between two staff points shall be determined by the level in its two different set ups on the same station. The two values shall agree within 0.9 mm.

5.2.2 Field Test of Collimation - The collimation shall be tested in the field by making observations on appropriate staves at equal and unequal The two staves shall be placed 80 m apart and the instrument distances. shall be placed in the middle of the line, that is at 40 m from each staff. The difference in heights of the two staff points, say X, shall be determined The instrument shall then be shifted to another point in in this situation. the line such that the distance of one staff is 20 m while that of the other staff is 60 m from the instrument; retaining the staves precisely on their original points. The difference in heights, say 2'-, of the two staff points shall again be determined in this situation. In case, there is no collimation error, the height difference as determined in both the positions of the instrument shall remain the same within a tolerance of 1.2 mm. Beyond this limit, the collimation error shall be corrected as follows: For this, the instrument ( at this position of unequal staff distances ) shall be focussed on the farther staff, say B, and the horizontal wire is made to intersect the farther staff B at original reading + ( Y - X) x f by means of micrometer screw. This will disturb the bubble which should be brought to the centre of its run by means of capstan or square head screws at the end of the bubble tube. 5.2.3 Field Test for Determination of Standard Deviation - The standard deviation ( error ) of the level shall be determined by the test method given in Appendix A. 5.3 Climatic
and Environmental Tests 5.3.0 The following tests shall be carried on as given in IS : 2352-1863*. These are only type approval tests to be carried on sample basis as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. These are not to be used in routine testing during bulk production.

*Procedure for basic climatic and durability tests for optical instruments.

Es: 9613 - 1980
53.1 Temperature Test - The level shall be subjected to cold and dry heat test on severities - 10�C and 55�C respectively and checked thereafter for collimation, parallax, deterioration of cementing and antireflection coating. 5.3.2 Rain Test - The level, in its case, shall be tested in a rain chamber and after the test the level shall be checked for ingress of moisture or water drops and for deterioration to any part of the instrument. 5.3.3 Fungus ( Mould ) Growth Test - The level shall be tested for the fungus growth and checked thoroughly after the test. 5.3.4 Vtbration Test - The level, in its case, shall be clamped on to a vibration table giving approximately 450 vibrations per minute with an amplitude of 3 mm for a period of 5 minutes. After the test, the instrument shall be in perfect adjustment.
6. MARKING

6.1 The level shall be marked with the manufacturer's mark and the year of manufacture. 6.1.1

name

or trade Mark.

The level may also be marked with the IS1 Certification

NOTE- The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity Details of conditions under which a licence to that standard as a further safeguard. for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

7. PACKING 7.1 The level shall be placed in its case together with its accessories and also an instruction booklet containing the guidelines for its use and adjustment. The case shall be suitably packed for transit.

APPENDIX A ( Clause 5.2.3 )
METHOD OF TESTING STANDARD ( ERROR ) OF LEVEL DEVIATION

A-I. PROCEDURE A-I.1 In order to test for standard deviation, the following shall be fulfilled: a) Instrument concerned in good adjustment, b) Good staves and experienced staffmen, requirements

c) Good and experienced observers, d) Four test lines ( legs ) connecting at least four and maximum five bench marks, established by levelling of high precision. The length of each leg shall be 250 m so that the total length of levelling line may be 1 km. The bench marks shall be selected in such a way that the four differential heights may be between O-5 m to 2'5 m. A-l.2 The four test legs ( la, lb, I, and Zd) shall be used in either of the following patterns (p), (q) or (r) ( see Fig. 2 ).

(P)
Bi, B2, 63, B4, Bs

(9)
B'l, B'2, B's, FIG. 2
B'4, B's

(r)
BM1, BM2, BMs, BM4

BI, BP, BB, Bq, Bg, B'I, B'z, B'S) B'4, B';, BMI, BM,, BM, and BM4 denotes the bench marks. It may bie seen that patterns (p) and (q) shall involve five bench marks while (I) shall involve only four bench marks.

Is : 9613 - 1980
A-l.3 On each test leg five fore and five back levellings shall be carried on so that 10 differential heights may be observed. The mean of these measurements shall be calculated and deviations of each value from the mean found out. The squares of deviations shall be taken and sum of such 10 squares of deviations shall be found out in case of each leg. These shall be denoted as Cz&,, %slb, EN, and Zvsld. If I;vs is denoted as the sum of the squares of deviations on four legs, then I;vs = XL+?,+ I;&, + Zvsl, + Zvsla. The standard deviation shall be calculated by the formula: S per km of double levelling X&d: A-2. PRECAUTIONS A-2.1 While carrying out the above test the following precautions shall be observed: a) The discordance between the fore and back values shall be kept within the specified tolerance for that particular type of level. b) All usual precauti,ons and errors shall be strictly taken into consideration.
